newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses rangebound, EMU optimism curbs gains.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses rangebound, EMU optimism curbs gains.

text.p: The mark looked set to remain rangebound on crosses after coming under earlier pressure amid renewed confidence in Europe's monetary union, analysts said.

The mark, which slipped to its lowest levels in four months against the lira early on Tuesday, rebounded off lows on European crosses after a remark from a French minister rattled positive sentiment over the euro.

But economists said the comment was not sufficient to shake off the market's confidence in a timely EMU start, after EU ministers meeting in Amsterdam reached accord on Monday on a key pact designed to ensure budgetary discipline after EMU's launch.

French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici gave a boost to the lagging German unit when he said an assessment of the state of public finances in France over the next six months would be crucial in reaching a decision over the country's signing up to the single currency.
But a trader at a Japanese bank in London said the mark was still seen as a sell.

"That comment (by Moscovici) just added another element of uncertainty to EMU and the mark was bought up right away," he said. "But after yesterday, the mark is still looking like a sell in general ... it didn't rebound very much."
By midday in Europe the Mark was still weak on most crosses.
Mark/French franc was changing hands at 3.3733/38 compared to 3.3735/40 late on Monday, while mark/peseta was down to 84.40/42 versus 84.45/47.
"In general the mark is going to remain fairly weak today and for the rest of the week," said Ernesto Ramirez, European economist at Bankers Trust in London.
"But these levels should be about the lowest we'll see - especially mark/lira."
The lira surged to touch 975.75 against the mark as dealers reacted to the fresh wave of confidence in the EMU timetable.
Dealers in Milan said the Bank of Italy might be tempted to step in and buy the German currency.
By midday in Europe the mark had rebounded slightly to trade at 978.35/65 lira compared to 981.3/981.6 late Monday.

As Italian government bonds also rallied, Bankers Trusts' Ramirez noted it was still too early to bet on Italy being included in a 1999 start to the single currency. "The lira will still have some trouble meeting the entry criteria for EMU," he said.
The mark also struggled against the Norwegian crown, which recovered from overnight lows as the Norwegian central bank said it would give up self-imposed curbs on forex intervention.
